examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне/вам хочется = I/you feel like, really want

examples.text: Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: Самсоновы, ну вы очнитесь! Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: Samsonovs, come to your senses! I understand you really want the flat.

meanings.en: to value, to appreciate, to esteem
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to value, to appreciate', paired with 'оценить'.

examples.text: Город высоко ценит вас и вашего мужа.
examples.trans: The city values you and your husband highly.

examples.text: Слушай, Лёля, я очень ценю, что ты приехала.
examples.trans: Listen, Lyolya, I really appreciate that you came.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Я что-то вижу = I see something. Core Russian pron meaning 'something; somehow' in everyday speech.
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
